contacts.angle: Our Thesis (20x Math Innovation Gap) + Free Spatial Labs
contacts.subject_line: Aligning on the 20x Math Innovation Gap: Twisted23 Spatial Lab & Gravity Wizards (Anchorage, AK)
contacts.custom_blurb: Hi Carina Initiatives & Thinking Games team, Your thesis—that early mathematical and spatial ability strongly predicts future innovation, yet decades of cuts to public gifted and acceleration tracks have created a 20-fold gap in invention rates and left a 10–55% boost in national innovation on the table—is the exact North Star behind our work here in Anchorage, Alaska. We build free digital spatial-reasoning gyms (https://twisted23.com & https://flippingdice.twisted23.com) and low-cost, hands-on physics kits (https://gravitywizards.com) so working- and middle-class families don't have to wait on gated programs. We would love to share our ecosystem (Flipping Dice 3D-in-2D Die Lab, Twisted 23, Tophat Sudoku, and Gravity Wizards FOBBs) for consideration in the Thinking Games catalog.
contacts.notes: Sent Nov 11 from iCloud prior to Resend setup.

contacts.subject_line: Database submission + Puzzle archaeology & 3D-in-2D cube geometry (Tophat Sudoku & Flipping Dice)
contacts.custom_blurb: Hi Thinky Games team, I was reading your 'How we choose what to cover' guidelines and loved your focus on subjective team curiosity and pure puzzle mechanics, so I wanted to submit our browser-playable spatial lab (https://flippingdice.twisted23.com) to your database and share two interconnected stories: (1) Flipping Dice & The 3D-in-2D Die Geometry Lab—encoding all 24 valid cube orientations (opposite faces = 7) directly onto a 2D face (TF = Top * 10 + Front) with an Untimed Thinky Mode, Axle-Locked (7-1-7-5) Learning Lab, and embedded 24-slot diagonal Twisted 23 puzzle; and (2) Rescuing Tophat Sudoku by tapping the orphaned Flash database of tophatpuzzle.com after its developer Domas vanished, and fixing its logic to guarantee unique solutions.

contacts.angle: Local Feature: Anchorage Inventor Rescues Lost Flash Game & Builds FOBBs
contacts.subject_line: Local Feature Pitch: The Anchorage inventor who tapped a vanished dev's Flash database—and reinvented the Pinewood Derby
contacts.custom_blurb: Hi Nathaniel, Here’s an offbeat Anchorage creator story connecting internet puzzle archaeology, bouncing rockets, and a 20-fold national math gap: When the developer (Domas) of the old Flash puzzle tophatpuzzle.com vanished, I tapped the abandoned database from here in Anchorage, fixed its non-unique solution flaw as Tophat Sudoku (https://twisted23.com), launched our browser-based 3D-in-2D Die Lab (https://flippingdice.twisted23.com), and founded Gravity Wizards (https://gravitywizards.com) using trackless bouncing FOBBs.

contacts.angle: Grassroots DIY STEM: Reimagining Pinewood Derbies with Bouncing FOBBs
contacts.subject_line: Project Spotlight: Ditching the Pinewood Derby track for bouncing gravity FOBBs + a 3D-in-2D spatial geometry trainer
contacts.custom_blurb: Hi Make: Editorial & Community team, Every maker knows the classic Pinewood Derby—and its biggest limitation: needing a 40-foot track. In Anchorage, Alaska, we launched Gravity Wizards (https://gravitywizards.com) to put everyday families first by replacing the track with FOBBs (Flying Objects Built to Bounce), alongside our free Axle-Locked (7-1-7-5) 3D-in-2D Cube Geometry Trainer at https://flippingdice.twisted23.com/learning-lab/.
